entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant/claimant, who sustained injuries in a road traffic accident on 29.12.2012, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, seeking compensation amount of Rs.2,00,000/-.
The Tribunal after considering the entire evidence on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,21,000/- with interest at the rate of 8% p.a.
Being aggrieved with the quantum of compensation, the claimant is before this Court.
NC: 2025:KHC:30848 HC-KAR 3.
Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the respondent - Insurance Company and perused the records.

4. It is stated that as per Ex.P.7-wound certificate, injuries sustained by the claimant is grievous in nature but the Tribunal has awarded lesser amount under the head pain and sufferings, and under the head food nourishment, attendant & transportation charges are also lower in side.
Under the head loss of earnings is also very meager.

Therefore, the claimant requests for enhancement of compensation with interest @ of 12% p.a.
5.
As per Ex.P.7-Wound Certificate, the claimant has sustained fracture of tooth, mouth and multiple small abrasions over face.
Ex.P.13 is the discharge summary.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries sustained amount of Rs.40,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal under the head pain and sufferings.

6. Taking into account the fact that the claimant has suffered fracture which is grievous in nature Mr. Nazeer Ahmed vs Mr. Raj Kumar on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45124399/
2 along with other simple injuries and that the claimant was an inpatient for 5 NC: 2025:KHC:30848 HC-KAR days, i.e., from 29.12.2012 to 04.01.2013.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I deem it appropriate to enhance the compensation under the head 'Pain and Suffering' by an additional sum of Rs.25,000/-.

7. Though medical bills are produced for a sum of Rs.94,387/- there was double bills for similar treatment, considering the same, the Tribunal has rightly awarded amount of Rs.36,000/- under the head Medical Expenses.
8. The accident occurred in the year 2012, and the claimant was aged 47 years at the time of the accident.
Injured was a driver.

In the absence of proof of income, the notional income is assessed at Rs.10,000/- , according to the chart prepared by the Karnataka Legal Services Authority, and income assessed by the Tribunal is at Rs.10,000/- per month which needs no interference.

9. Considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the claimant, and the period of hospitalization,
the sum of Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards Food, nourishment attendant and transportation is deemed insufficient and is therefore enhanced by an additional Rs.20,000/-,
bringing the total to Rs.30,000/- under this head.
Given the nature of the injuries and functional disability, the Tribunal's decision requires a review to ensure just compensation for the claimant.

Medical Expenses : Rs. 36,000/-
 Loss of Amenities : Rs. 25,000/-
 Food and nourishment, Rs. 30,000/-
 conveyance  And attendant charges)
 Loss of income during laid up : Rs. 10,000/-
 period  TOTAL : Rs. 1,66,000/-
 11.
Therefore, the appellant is awarded a total compensation of Rs.1,66,000/- as opposed to the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.1,21,000/-.
The appellant is entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.45,000/-, along with interest at 8% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till its actual realization.

ii. The appellant - claimant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.45,000/-,
along with interest at 8% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till deposit in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

iii. The enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest is to be released in favour of the claimant by the respondent - Insurance Company within a period of one month from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order.
